Serializing your classes

ParquetSerializer (package ParquetNeo.Serialization) writes the properties of your classes and records as columns and reads them back.

using ParquetNeo.Serialization;

ParquetSerializer.Serialize(rows, stream, new ParquetSerializerOptions
{
    RowGroupSize = 100_000,        // rows in a row group: the unit that is read, skipped, and compressed together
    MaxDegreeOfParallelism = 4,    // columns of a row group are encoded on this many threads; the bytes do not depend on it
    Writer = new ParquetWriterOptions { Compression = CompressionCodec.Gzip },
});

What maps to a column

Single columns: numbers, decimal, bool, strings, byte arrays, Guid, the date and time types (DateOnly, TimeOnly, DateTime, DateTimeOffset), enums, and the nullable forms of those. Around them:

  • Nested objects and structs, to any depth, become groups.
  • Arrays, lists, sets and other collections become LIST columns, and dictionaries become MAPs.
  • A property is optional (it may be null in the file) when its type is nullable: int?, string? with nullable reference types on, and so on.
  • Records and classes with a constructor that has parameters are read by calling that constructor with the values of the properties it names.

The columns are matched with the properties by name when reading, so the file may have more columns than the class, and a column that the class does not have is not read.

Adjusting the mapping

Attributes in ParquetNeo.DataModel change how a property is stored:

Attribute Effect
[ParquetColumn("name")] The name of the column, or its position among the columns
[ParquetIgnore] The property is not written or read
[ParquetDecimal(precision, scale)] The precision and scale of a decimal (the default is 38 and 18)
[ParquetTime(unit)], [ParquetTimestamp(...)] The unit and meaning of the column of a time or of a date and time
[ParquetEncoding(encoding)] The encoding of the values of the column (PLAIN by default)
[ParquetDictionary(mode)] Whether the column has a dictionary: on, off, or decided by what the values look like

Reading a big file

Deserialize returns a list. DeserializeAll and DeserializeAllAsync give the rows one row group at a time, so memory is bounded by the largest row group:

foreach (var row in ParquetSerializer.DeserializeAll<Person>(stream))
{
    // ...
}

To read less of the file, give a filter: see Skipping what is not needed.
